faq.q: Why does a diesel engine draw in only air?
faq.a: If fuel were mixed in early, it would catch fire too soon as the air was squeezed. Injecting it at the top of the stroke controls exactly when it burns.
asks: When is the fuel added in a diesel?

faq.q: Why does squeezing air make it hot?
faq.a: Pushing a piston into a gas does work on it, and that energy makes the gas molecules move faster. Faster molecules means a higher temperature.
asks: Why does a bike pump get warm?

faq.q: How hot does the air get in a diesel engine?
faq.a: Squeezed hard, the air reaches roughly 500 to 800 degrees Celsius, well above the temperature at which diesel fuel catches fire by itself.
asks: What temperature does diesel ignite at?

faq.q: What does a diesel injector do?
faq.a: The injector sprays fuel at very high pressure, often more than 1,000 times atmospheric pressure, as a fine mist. Tiny droplets mix with the hot air and burn quickly.
On a cold morning the cold engine metal cools the air as it is squeezed, so it may not get hot enough to light the fuel. Glow plugs are small electric heaters that warm each cylinder for starting.
asks: Why are diesels hard to start in the cold?

facts: Diesel engines are called compression-ignition engines.
Modern diesel injectors spray fuel at more than 1,000 times atmospheric pressure.
Glow plugs help diesel engines start in cold weather.

quiz.why: The injector sprays fuel into air already made hot by squeezing, so it lights at once.

wrong.1: That is how most petrol engines work; in a diesel it would ignite too early.
wrong.2: After the exhaust stroke the cylinder fills with fresh air, not fuel.

quiz.say: Why does a bicycle pump get warm when you use it?
quiz.show: Why does a bicycle pump get warm when you use it?
quiz.why: Doing work on a gas by squashing it raises its temperature, the same effect a diesel uses.

wrong.1: Your hand adds a little warmth, but the main cause is squeezing the air.
wrong.2: The heat comes from the pump squeezing air, not the tyre.
